_about: Planning factors for the MODEL step. Every value has a source or is marked team_assumption. Edit here, not in code. Counties and DHS are expected to replace assumptions with their own figures.

shelter_seeking_rate._about: Share of the at-risk population expected to use a public shelter. low / central / high.

hurricane.source: South Carolina EMD, 2026 Hurricane Response Annex G (planning factors 2%, 3%, 5%)

wildfire.source: high = observed Maui 2023: 1,418 people in shelters on Aug 11, 2023 (Maui Now) / Lahaina CDP population 12,702 (2020 Census). low and central are team_assumption.

tsunami.source: team_assumption: central 5%; low 2% = hurricane planning factor (SCEMD); high 11% = observed Maui 2023 no-notice total-loss rate

inland_flood.source: team_assumption: central 5%; low 2% = hurricane planning factor (SCEMD); high 11% = observed Maui 2023 no-notice total-loss rate

coastal_flood.source: team_assumption: central 5%; low 2% = hurricane planning factor (SCEMD); high 11% = observed Maui 2023 no-notice total-loss rate

footprint._about: Which tracts are at risk in each planning scenario. County totals assume every at-risk tract is hit at once: an upper planning bound. Use needs_by_tract.csv to plan for one community.

tsunami.note: Population share inside the State standard tsunami evacuation zone. Extreme zone is reported separately.

footprint.nri_top_share_note: NRI ratings are national, so few or very many Hawaiʻi tracts rate High. Footprint = top 25% of Hawaiʻi tracts by NRI risk score, scores above 0 only (team_assumption).

floor_sqft_72h.source: Florida DEM Sheltering Guidance Aid (2010): emergency evacuation shelter, <=72 h

meals_per_day.source: Florida DEM (2010): two hot meals a day plus snacks

persons_per_toilet_72h.source: Florida DEM (2010): emergency evacuation shelter, <=72 h

staff_per_shift._about: One staff member per N shelter residents, minimum 1 when the shelter is open. Florida DEM (2010) staffing metrics; the source marks them as recommendations.

dog_owning_household_share.source: AVMA U.S. pet ownership statistics (2020 data)

afn_composition_note: Shelter residents are assumed to mirror their tract's CMIST rates. Research and DHS both indicate people with AFN are more likely to need public shelter, so AFN counts in shelter are a floor, not a ceiling.
